<!-- pr-reviewer: d1dc959b69249d681a26b0916fa2f91e82d012cd -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Tolerance is rounding-scale and stated in units: `TOUCH` = 1e-9 mm (1 pm), `guard.rs`, with the reasoning (f64 rounding at 1e4 mm ~1e-12, i.e. 1000x below; cutting tolerances are microns, 1e6x above). The test is a distance (`|orient| <= TOUCH*|ab|`), so it does not shrink or grow with chord length, and it needs no division.
- Strict opposite-sides on both chords is kept, so a real crossing still crosses. Only the old exact zero was widened.
- Safer than before: non-finite points (NaN, inf in x or y) now read as a crossing instead of being dropped by the length filter or passed by an x-only bounds check.
- Pinned both ways: rounding-apart shared ends, a landing on a chord end and a ring starting on the last ring's vertex are not crossings (each also asserts the old exact `proper` tripped, so the knife edge is exercised). A crossing 0.15 mm past a shared vertex, and a vertex 1e-6 mm through a chord, still cross. A grid-vs-all-pairs test covers the bucketing.
- No unwrap/expect/panic added. `proper` is untouched for `lift_link`. Provenance line updated; files small. Decision file present, `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1048` present, no process files, no snapshots, no build.rs/deps.

**Local results (PR head trial-merged with upstream/main: merged cleanly, no conflicts; macOS arm64)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| motion lib | 202 passed, 1 ignored (9 guard tests incl.) |
| motion adaptive_hsm / adaptive_band / adaptive_orbit_seam / rotary_adaptive / trochoid_slot (debug) | 1 / 2 / 1 / 3 / 10 passed |
| release `--ignored`: adaptive_hsm | 5 passed (incl. island budget, M11.4 report) |
| release `--ignored`: rotary_adaptive | 3 passed (r6.2 neck refusals still by name) |
| release `--ignored`: motion pocket3d_hsm | 1 passed |
| app pocket3d_hsm bore (release, ignored, exact) | passed; moves 16160 / planar 15432 / arcs 1571, identical to the macOS pin |
| app golden_cl | 25 passed |
| clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings | clean |

No plan, golden or count changed: every pinned plan/count assertion (60x14 slot, 60x40 island, r6.2 neck, bore counts) holds. I did not build main side by side to diff unpinned output, so "no flip" rests on those pins.

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The "just past the tolerance" pin is at 1e-6 mm for a vertex through a chord; a case at ~2e-9 mm (just beyond `TOUCH`) would pin the edge itself. The 5e-10 mm contact case covers the inside edge.
- #1129: the verifier's law (a) is still exact-sign, so the planner and verifier can disagree on a rounding-apart end. Safe direction (refused by name), as the PR says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 0f2f42179a80d149468669f853aeabb4053b70bd -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The earlier finding is fixed. The guard now uses the same end-point-only rule and the same 1e-9 mm value as main's verifier (`proper_cross_touch`, PR #1308). Every real crossing I probed above the tolerance is still reported.

Reviewed at head `0f2f4217`, trial-merged locally with `origin/main` `fe1cb894`. The merge was clean and was not pushed. Windows 11, x86_64.

### Earlier finding (NeoTech review at `d1dc959b`)
1. *A walk passing through a chord at a vertex within `TOUCH` of that chord's interior must be reported.* **Fixed.**
   - `side()` (`guard.rs:46-59`) now excuses a point only when it is within `TOUCH` (a `hypot` distance) of one of the other chord's **end points**. Everywhere else the exact orientation sign decides.
   - `crosses()` (`:70-77`) is `s1*s2 < 0 && s3*s4 < 0`. That is the same predicate as `sim/verify/laws.rs::proper_cross_touch`: all four sides non-zero and opposite in pairs.
   - The probe `(2,1) -> (2,±0.5e-9) -> (2,-1)` through `(0,0)-(4,0)` reports again, at four origins up to 1 m. It is pinned by `a_walk_through_a_chord_at_a_vertex_a_picometre_off_its_line_still_crosses`.
   - The claims I asked to correct ("no self-cut can hide inside it", "at most a 1 pm overlap") are gone from the `TOUCH` doc comment and from `docs/decisions/1048-guard-shared-ends.md`. The decision file records the withdrawn rule and the residual it leaves.

### What looks good
- **Same rule as the verifier.** End points only, 1e-9 mm, point-to-point, with no blur of the orientation test. There is one deliberate difference: a non-finite point always crosses here, which is the safe reading for a planner. The verifier keeps its exact reading for those.
- **`proper` is unchanged** for `lift_link`. The guard's production readers are `pocket_hsm::adaptive_passes` (a crossing falls back to Offset rings by name), `pocket_troch` (refuses the trochoid) and `lift::coarsen` (`crossing_pairs` keeps the fine chords).
- **Pins work both ways.** Each knife-edge pin asserts that the old `proper` really tripped. The bucketed scan is checked against all pairs. Contacts are pinned exactly: a T-touch, a collinear overlap and a retrace (the retrace is what `a_channel_is_grown_as_one_spiral_that_never_crosses` needs).
- **Code and process checks.**
  - No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.
  - `guard.rs` is 164 lines and `guard_tests.rs` 236.
  - The provenance line is updated.
  - `Fixes #1048` and a `Changelog:` line are present.
  - No process files, snapshots, goldens, `build.rs` or dependency changes.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` | 210 passed, 1 ignored (guard: 9 tests) |
| motion `adaptive_band` / `adaptive_hsm` / `adaptive_orbit_seam` / `machining2d` / `offset_shells` / `pocket3d_hsm` / `rotary_adaptive` / `tiny_step` / `trochoid_slot` (debug) | 2 / 1 (+5 ign) / 1 / 66 / 6 (+1 ign) / 3 (+1 ign) / 3 (+3 ign) / 3 / 10, all ok |
| app `golden_cl` | 26 passed |
| app `conformance` / `pick_agnostic` / `pocket3d_hsm` / `roughing2d` / `shoulder_adaptive` / `trochoid_op` / `whole_model_pocket` | 6 / 5 (+2 ign) / 1 (+1 ign) / 7 / 3 / 5 / 5, all ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the release `--ignored` heavy lanes (the author reports them green on Linux at this rule's first head), UI and snapshots (untouched).

**Goldens.** No golden file and no existing test expectation changed. `golden_cl` passes 26/26 on the merged tree.

### Probes (throwaway local tests, removed)
| Probe | Reported as crossing |
|---|---|
| walk vertex 1e-6 / 1e-8 / 2e-9 / 1.5e-9 / 1e-9 mm past a lap's END, walk passing through | yes, all |
| same at 5e-10 mm (inside `TOUCH` of the end) | no (the intended touch) |
| chord crossing a lap 1e-6 / 1e-8 / 2e-9 / 5e-10 mm from the lap's end (no vertex near) | yes, all |
| 1e4 mm lap crossed 1 / 1e-6 / 2e-9 mm from its far end; 1e4 mm slanted lap crossed 1e-6 mm from its end | yes, all |
| walk vertex ~2e-9 mm below the far end of a 1e4 mm lap, passing through | yes |
| T exactly on the interior / 2e-9 mm past it | no / yes |
| collinear overlap | no (unchanged from exact-sign) |
| walk with a 0.6 pm chord straddling a lap's interior | yes |
| lap carrying a 0.5 pm chord, crossed 1e-6 / 2.5e-9 mm beside it | yes / yes (a tiny move excuses no neighbour) |
| tiny walk chord just above the line, then its neighbour crosses | yes |
| nearly parallel pass-through, 1e-9 rad over 1000 mm | yes |
| nearly parallel chord leaving 0.5 pm / 2 pm off the lap's start, diverging | no / yes |
| zero-length chords only; empty walk | no; no |
| NaN walk | yes |
| `TOUCH == crate::verify::CROSSING_TOUCH` (from motion) | compiles, equal |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **One constant instead of two.** Today `TOUCH` is a local literal. Its doc comment (`guard.rs:19-20`) and the decision file say "no motion -> sim dependency". That is not so: `camcraft-motion` already depends on `camcraft-sim` (`crates/motion/Cargo.toml:11`) and re-exports `verify` (`crates/motion/src/lib.rs:40`). `CROSSING_TOUCH` is `pub` there, and my probe `assert_eq!(TOUCH, crate::verify::CROSSING_TOUCH)` compiles in motion. The cross-crate pin the #1308 review asked for is therefore one line:
   ```rust
   pub(super) const TOUCH: f64 = crate::verify::CROSSING_TOUCH;
   ```
   Alternatively, add that `assert_eq!` as a test. Then correct the "no dependency" sentence in both places. If the two constants drift in either direction, the verifier still refuses the post by name, so this is not a safety blocker.
2. **An X exactly through a shared vertex reads as a touch.** A walk that passes straight through another walk's **vertex**, within 1 pm of it, is not reported. Probe: `(4,±1)` through lap vertex `(4,0)` at 0 and 0.5 pm, crossing (no); at 2 pm, crossing (yes). The PR pins this itself: `a_return_landing_on_a_chord_end_does_not_cross`, `back = (6,-4)` -> `lap[1]` -> `(7,3)` crosses the lap at that vertex. This is the same reading as an exactly shared vertex under exact-sign and as main's verifier, and the decision file names it as the residual. Mentioned so the maintainer sees that it is now consistent in both the planner and the verifier, with no backstop between them for that one case.
3. **The PR body is stale.** It still describes the withdrawn line-band rule ("within `TOUCH` of the other chord's line", `|orient| <= TOUCH * |ab|`, "a chord end within 1 pm of a line can only meet the other chord at that end"). The `Changelog:` line is fine. The body's "What changed" and "The tolerance and why" sections should be updated to the end-point rule, so the merge record matches the code.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
